review_context: EPLI carrier-assignment executable fixture expansion and L&E budget-driver QA refresh.
finding_title: L&E critical budget facts need separate states for missing versus source-present but unconfirmed.
finding_summary: The current executable fact-binding layer treats critical facts as blockers without a first-class distinction between facts absent from source material and facts present in source material but still requiring human confirmation. That makes carrier/client/insured role evidence hard to model for nonblocking range-only or candidate-range cases.
observable_context: New synthetic EPLI fixtures include carrier, TPA, payer, insured, represented-client, claimant, and opposing-counsel signals.
The clean EPLI fixture has source text naming the relevant role candidates but still requires human confirmation before budget use.
The current fact-binding manifest can safely bind noncritical expected gaps, but binding critical role facts would make the downstream blocked-driver review treat the case as amount-budget-blocked.

The implementation therefore left critical role facts unbound in these nonblocking fixtures and used noncritical driver facts such as expert/vendor needs and forum/arbitration posture to exercise the budget-output partition.
observable_decision_logic: Missing critical facts should block amount-budget output before proposal.
Source-present but unconfirmed critical role facts should remain candidate-only and human-gated, but they should not be indistinguishable from missing facts.
The budget QA chain needs to know whether a blocker is absence of evidence, role ambiguity, or human-confirmation pending state.
DAD should classify this as a recurring issue pattern because legal-budget workflows will repeatedly face present-but-unconfirmed carrier, insured, employer, claimant, and affiliate relationships.
solution_path: Add a candidate fact state such as source_present_needs_confirmation or review_only_critical_fact beside missing_critical_fact.
Update fact-binding, driver-binding, blocked-driver review, budget-output expectations, and UI labels to preserve the distinction.
Add synthetic tests where role evidence is present but unconfirmed and the allowed budget output is range-only or candidate-range pending review.
Map the states to separate candidate Exception Lake labels so DAD can distinguish missing intake evidence from human-confirmation pressure.
applies_when: A source packet contains role or budget-driver evidence but the workflow still requires human confirmation before pricing.
A critical fact should affect budget output posture but should not be treated the same as missing evidence.
Carrier, insured, employer, claimant, affiliate, joint-employer, or payer relationships are present in source text but unresolved for review.
does_not_apply_when: The source packet truly lacks the critical fact.
A human confirmation artifact has already resolved the role or driver fact.
The fact is noncritical and only widens ranges or creates assumptions.
danger_if_misapplied: If source-present critical facts are treated as resolved, the budget may overstate confidence. If they are treated as missing, the system may over-block useful range-only review packets and hide evidence that reviewers need.
suggested_actions: DAD should classify this as a candidate exception-pattern and learning-loop issue for L&E budget-driver state modeling.
DAD should ask Exception Lake design to preserve separate labels for missing fact, ambiguous fact, and source-present pending-confirmation fact.
Codex should implement the candidate fact-state split in a future PR before expanding high-risk L&E executable fixtures.
reviewer_notes: This record contains synthetic fixture and artifact references only.
It records observable rationale and implementation constraints, not hidden chain-of-thought.
red_team_notes: Do not let the UI display source-present critical facts as human-confirmed facts.
Do not let a future Lake mapping merge missing evidence and confirmation-pending evidence into one undifferentiated event.
